message.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Two partial orders on a reflection group
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mi>W</mml:mi>
                    </mml:math>
                    , the
                    <jats:italic>codimension order</jats:italic>
                    and the
                    <jats:italic>prefix order</jats:italic>
                    , are together called the
                    <jats:italic>absolute order</jats:italic>
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Abs</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>W</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    when they agree. We show that in this case the absolute order on a complex reflection group has the strong Sperner property, except possibly for the Coxeter group of type
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:msub>
                        <mml:mi>D</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mi>n</mml:mi>
                      </mml:msub>
                    </mml:math>
                    , for which this property is conjectural. The Sperner property had previously been established for the
                    <jats:italic>
                      noncrossing partition lattice
                      <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                        <mml:mrow>
                          <mml:mi>N</mml:mi>
                          <mml:msub>
                            <mml:mi>C</mml:mi>
                            <mml:mi>W</mml:mi>
                          </mml:msub>
                        </mml:mrow>
                      </mml:math>
                    </jats:italic>
                     [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">11</jats:xref>
                    ,
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">13</jats:xref>
                    ], a certain maximal interval in
                    <mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi mathvariant="normal">Abs</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                        <mml:mi>W</mml:mi>
                        <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math>
                    , but not for the entire poset, except in the case of the symmetric group [
                    <jats:xref ref-type="bibr">8</jats:xref>
                    ]. We also show that neither the codimension order nor the prefix order has the Sperner property for general complex reflection groups.
                  </jats:p>
title: On the Sperner property for the absolute order on complex reflection groups
